subject: Cognitive Science
title: Bayesian Thinking
description: A fast breakdown of Bayesian Thinking for builders.

hook.text: You believe there's a 30% chance it'll rain. Then you see dark clouds. How should your estimate change?

buildup.text: Bayes' theorem gives the exact answer: update your prior belief with new evidence to get a better estimate.

discovery.text: Good forecasters think this way: start with a base rate, then nudge it with each new piece of information.

twist.text: Most people overreact to dramatic evidence and underreact to quiet statistical evidence. We're bad Bayesians.

climax.text: Philip Tetlock found that 'superforecasters' beat intelligence agencies by consistently applying Bayesian updates.

punchline.text: Update in small steps. Never be 100% sure of anything.

details.summary: Bayesian thinking updates beliefs by combining prior knowledge with new evidence. When a medical test is positive, the true probability of disease depends not just on test accuracy but also on how common the disease is. Humans are notoriously bad at intuitive Bayesian reasoning.
details.whyItMatters: Bayesian reasoning is the gold standard for rational belief updating. Understanding it prevents common errors in medical, legal, and everyday probability judgments.
takeaways: Prior probability must be combined with new evidence
Base rates dramatically affect the meaning of test results
Humans systematically neglect priors in Bayesian tasks

faq.question: Why do people misinterpret medical test results?
faq.answer: A test that is 95 percent accurate for a disease affecting 1 in 1000 people still produces mostly false positives. People focus on the test accuracy and ignore the low base rate. When priors are low, even highly accurate tests produce surprising numbers of false positives.

faq.question: How can Bayesian thinking be taught effectively?
faq.answer: Natural frequency formats work better than percentages. Instead of saying one percent base rate, say 10 out of 1000 people have the disease. Visual aids like frequency trees also dramatically improve performance. The math is the same, but the format makes it intuitive.
